method: AI-assisted inspection of public publisher, journal and repository pages on 2026-10-05. Bibliographic corroboration only; not a full-text factual review.

doiTitleVariants.note: Publisher includes the subtitle omitted from the Crossref main-title field.
Publisher includes the subtitle A study of the UK and German Euro elections; main title and authors match.
Journal confirms review designation, title, authors and 2022 publication. It is a book review, not the original study described in the reviewed book.
Publisher confirms full title and 2024. Chad Raphael and Martha Matsuoka are editors; Crossref author field missing is not an invented author.

otherChecks.note: Cambridge confirms Elinor Ostrom, the full book title, online ISBN 9781316423936 and 2015 edition. The 2015 date is not the original publication year.

GIGA confirms authors and 2013 working paper230. Captured metadata says article and publisher Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; original producer identifies it as a GIGA working paper. Existence does not validate the app's format/publisher label.

Repository confirms Ronald Walters interview material about the 1958 Wichita sit-in. It does not establish a direct Greensboro 1960 primary source. Catalog release date 2016 was not independently checked.

GovInfo confirms the hearing and June15,2023 event date. It is a hearing, not an introductory monograph. The catalog's 2026 publication date is a separate field and was not validated by the event date.

Cambridge lists the book by Joseph Vogel with online2012, print2010 and ISBN9781843318781. Anthem's contents identify chapter2's expanded title. Ranks3 and4 share the book ISBN and same chapter despite title/date variants. They should be grouped as one work. Rank3's2012 date corresponds to online publication; it is not fabricated merely because Crossref lists2010. This chapter is not Hardin's original1968 article.

limitations: No blanket accuracy claim is made for all fields or no-DOI records. Several no-DOI records were not independently corroborated. No full text, source credibility, peer-review process, access entitlement, or AI narrative claims were graded. Zero unregistered DOIs in this sample does not prove zero hallucinations.
